facts.text: This article was originally published as Switzerland Approves Crypto Tax Data Sharing With 57 Jurisdictions on Crypto Breaking News – your trusted source for crypto news, Bitcoin news, and blockchain updates.
Switzerland’s Federal Council has approved 57 potential partner jurisdictions for the automatic exchange of information related to crypto assets, with the process set to begin in 2028.
The decision is designed to broaden how far Swiss tax authorities can reach across borders when investigating taxpayers’ crypto activity.

Switzerland’s original plan contemplated implementing crypto tax information requirements in 2026, but lawmakers had not finalized which counterpart jurisdictions would be involved—an uncertainty that contributed to a delay of at least one year, according to earlier reporting from Cointelegraph .
For readers, the key point is that Switzerland’s 57-jurisdiction approval doesn’t operate in isolation.

It increases the number of places where Swiss tax data could potentially be reflected or acted upon—depending on each jurisdiction’s willingness to participate and its ability to meet the standards for confidentiality and data security.

For investors and businesses operating in multiple countries, the practical impact of Switzerland’s approval is straightforward: more jurisdictions become potential receivers of crypto-related tax data.
Switzerland has already built a foundation for automatic information exchange of financial account data.

That continuity matters for taxpayers and service providers because it suggests Switzerland intends to integrate crypto reporting into a broader transparency architecture rather than treating it as a one-off initiative.

Switzerland’s Federal Council has approved 57 potential partner jurisdictions for the automatic exchange of information related to Crypto Assets , paving the way for broader international tax cooperation beginning in 2028.
The decision marks a key step in the country’s adoption of new reporting standards and could give tax authorities greater visibility into cross-border activity involving Crypto Assets.
Under the revised plan, service providers handling Crypto Assets may begin collecting relevant customer data on Jan.
The new rules covering Crypto Assets are designed to address transparency gaps that traditional financial reporting mechanisms may not capture.
However, Switzerland said it will only exchange information with jurisdictions that formally express interest and meet international standards for confidentiality and data security.
Switzerland introduced the legal framework for exchanging financial account information in 2017 .
The reporting rules are based on the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework , commonly known as CARF.
